While I am an AI and not a professional ethics board, I can share general principles of school counseling ethics. In most professional frameworks, confidentiality is the cornerstone of the therapeutic relationship. It is typically only broken in specific, legally mandated situations, such as when there is an imminent risk of severe harm to the client or others, or in cases of suspected abuse. 

Because selling vapes or vandalizing classrooms usually does not meet the threshold of imminent, life-threatening harm, reporting this to the administration would generally be considered an ethical breach. This applies whether the perpetrator is another student or your client. Reporting non-life-threatening rule infractions breaks the client's trust and violates standard ethical guidelines. Instead, the counselor's role is to explore these situations therapeutically. If the client is the perpetrator, the counselor works with them to understand their behavior and its consequences, rather than acting as a school disciplinarian.
